newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish telecom firm TPSA seeks Q4 1998 listing.
newsitem.headline: Polish telecom firm TPSA seeks Q4 1998 listing.

text.p: State-owned Polish telecommunications monopoly Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) is seeking to enter the Warsaw bourse around the fourth quarter of 1998, the daily Rzeczpospolita reported on Saturday.

"The best time for our firm to enter the bourse would be the autumn of 1998," Rzeczpospolita quoted the company's deputy president Emil Plodzien as saying, adding the firm would more likely float a minority stake than seek a strategic investor.
"The experience of other telecoms shows that only the weakest of them with problems financing investment and development use the help of an investor," he said.
Plodzien said TPSA's privatisation should follow that of Germany's Deutsche Telekom AG and France Telecom, whose initial public offerings will take place this month and in April 1997 respectively.
The Polish government has said it expects to start TPSA's privatisation process next year.

Plodzien said TPSA, which was drafting privatisation plans with investment banks Schroders and CS First Boston, would likely form a holding in which the parent would take care of management and help direct the independenent subsidiaries.
But he said the privatisation should take place first.

Plodzien said TPSA, which was currently investing nearly $1 billion annually, would increase investment by about 15 percent over the next few years and lift its number of subscribers by 800,000 this year, 900,000 next year and one million in 1998.
TPSA had about 4.7 million subscribers at the start of this year in a country of nearly 40 million.

Plodzien said competition on the telecommunications market would steadily increase, with more than 150 local operators already receiving licences and the full opening of Poland's telecommunications market likely no sooner than 2003.
